name: And Furthermore—
premise: The name is not a name. It is the last word of every conversation you have ever lost. You turned to add one more point, the room had gone, and the only thing still listening had a trunk and infinite time. Sit with the arithmetic of that: how many rooms, over how many years, to earn a companion made entirely of your unfinished sentences.
conclusion: The conclusion is not flattering and it is not painful. It is simply that you have always talked to someone, and someone has always stayed.
effect_text: Rhetoric +1. Furthermore reaches you one notch more clearly.

name: The Sound of Typing
premise: Nobody in this building owns a typewriter. You have confirmed this. You have also confirmed that the sound occurs, that it occurs at intervals resembling composition rather than transcription — bursts, then pauses of exactly the length a person needs to reconsider a word — and that no resident finds this worth a second sentence.
conclusion: Somebody is working. The work has pauses in it. Pauses are where choices go.
effect_text: Logic +1. Typewriter evidence now grants a bonus on related checks.

name: The Presumptuousness of Senses
premise: If we are to believe the evidence of our senses — which, admittedly, seems rather presumptuous — then something here is deliciously askew. But the sentence has a second half you have been declining to write: if the senses are presumptuous, the presumption is yours, and the askewness is being performed for an audience of one.
conclusion: You are not being lied to by the world. You are being agreed with by it, constantly, and that is a far worse position to be in.
effect_text: Empathy +1, Logic -1. The town's agreeableness now reads as a symptom.

name: Hair of the Dog That Bit the Town
premise: Gin does not make Silvora Reefs more coherent. Gin makes you less bothered that it is not. There is a professional argument for this — a man who stops flinching at impossibilities can stand closer to them — and there is the other argument, which is that you have started making the professional argument.
conclusion: Both arguments are correct. That is the trouble with them.
effect_text: Electrochemistry +2, Physique -1. Intoxication penalties to Logic are halved.

name: The Man Who Is Your Name Backwards
premise: Snoino Revilo. Say it slowly. Then say your own, and say it slowly, and then say it in the other direction, which is a thing you have been able to do since you were eight and have never once had a reason to do since. Someone has your letters. They are using all of them and no others.
conclusion: An anagram is a coincidence. A reversal is an author.
effect_text: Savoir-Faire +1. Reversals and anagrams now yield more on examination.

name: Three Dry Pages
premise: The notebook went into the water with you. Every page is a blue smear except three, and those three are dry, and the handwriting on them is yours in the way a signature on a document you did not sign is yours. Water does not select. Water is the least selective thing there is.
conclusion: Something declined to let those three pages get wet. That is a preference. Preferences belong to people.
effect_text: Logic +1, Morale -5. You will not be putting the notebook down again.
